subject: Re: Production outage — elevated p99 and 503s after model v4.1/quant-q3 rollout

Cc: support@windward.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Prod impact after v4.1 (quant-q3) — urgent

Hi Nikhil,

We pushed live this morning on your guidance (v4.1, quant profile q3) and immediately started seeing large regressions across our inference tier. Quick summary: p50 is ~150ms (ok), p95 ~1.1s (up from 420ms), p99 ~3.7s (up from 720ms), and we're seeing 7-12% 503 errors for multi-turn chat flows. Throughput is down ~60% under our standard steady-state load.

This began at approximately 07:20 UTC and coincides with the rollout window you indicated. We rolled our clients back to the previous pinned model but the backend still serves the new variant for some routes. Attached are a handful of recent traces and sample requests (prod_p99_traces_20280403.log, request_samples.json).

This is causing our checkout flow to timeout and is blocking purchases. We need immediate remediation and an exec-level point of contact. Please advise rollback options, mitigation, and whether Redwood will cover short-term credits for the outage.

Thanks,
Lisa Carter
VP, Engineering — Windward Systems

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Prod impact after v4.1 (quant-q3) — urgent

Thanks for the flag and logs — I dug into the attached p99 traces. Quick technical readout (initial):
- Symptom: long stalls at attention kernel dispatch for long-context requests (1.2k–2.4k tokens). The quantized kernels in q3 are regressing throughput under multi-turn workloads due to increased memory traffic from the new tiled attention path.
- Error spikes (503) correlate with OOM/backpressure on the per-request worker pool when combined with our default batching heuristics.

Immediate mitigations I can push from the control plane (5–15 min):
1) Rollback routing: revert model alias for /api/chat/* to v4.0-fp16 for all inferred traffic (manual alias swap).
2) Hotfix config: reduce batch_size_max from 64 to 24 and force_kv_cache_prefetch = true to reduce memory bursts.
3) Quant fallback: switch quant-strategy 'q3' -> 'q3-safe' which prefers fp16 kernels for long-context (>1024 tokens) requests. This is a lightweight config flip and doesn't require model re-upload.

Risk & timeline: 1) Alias rollback is low risk and should restore prior p95/p99 in ~10–20m once routing converges. 2) Batch-size reduction will reduce throughput but will avoid 503s; expect throughput recover to ~85% of baseline. 3) Quant fallback reduces token-level perf but maintains correctness — recommended as an interim until we ship a tiled-attn patch.

I'll be on a dedicated channel and can execute the alias swap once we have customer confirmation. If we want automatic customer-visible rollback now, I can request an emergency change (requires PMO signoff) but I recommend the alias swap + q3-safe flip as fastest.

—Aditya Rao
Sr. Staff, Inference Runtime — Redwood Inference

- Manual alias rollback for /api/chat/* to v4.0-fp16 (will begin once you approve). Expected convergence 10–20m.
- Apply q3-safe quant fallback for long-context requests and reduce batch_size_max to 24 to reduce memory bursts. These are reversible and low risk.
- We'll keep the incident channel open, share live dashboards, and push updates every 15 minutes until stabilized.

Per Marissa's note, we will provisionally credit Windward 4 hours of inference spend for the impacted window; we will finalize amount after the postmortem.

Please reply with a single-line approval to proceed with the alias rollback and config flips. Once approved I will execute and post a status update.

Thanks — standing by.
